rule_metadata.description: The clear, distinct pronunciation of a vowelless Meem (مْ) without Ghunnah when followed by any of the 26 remaining alphabet letters (excluding Baa and Meem).

theoretical_foundation.linguistic_definition: Izhar means clarity and manifestation, and Shafawi means labial because the Meem exits from the lips.
theoretical_foundation.applied_tajweed_definition: When a non-vowelled Meem (مْ) is followed by any of the 26 letters (excluding ب and م) across words or within a word, the Meem is pronounced distinctly and clearly with its inherent sound, avoiding any nasal Ghunnah holding or merging.

critical_warning_waf_faa.rule: Proximity Warning with Fa (ف) and Waw (و)
critical_warning_waf_faa.explanation: Special care must be taken to pronounce the Meem clearly when followed by Waw or Fa. Because Waw and Fa share lip proximity with Meem, inexperienced reciters often mistakenly hide (Ikhfa) the Meem. The reciter must maintain strict clarity (Izhar).

theoretical_foundation.mushaf_indicator: The Meem Sakinah carries a clear Sukoon sign (مْ) above it.

practical_examples.breakdown: Clear pronunciation of Meem Sakinah before Lam without any nasal extension.
Critical Izhar warning: Pronounce the Meem of 'Alayhim' completely clear before Waw without letting it slip into Ikhfa.
Clear labial manifestation of Meem before Fa.
Clear Meem followed by throat letter Ha.

assessment_bank.question: How many letters trigger Izhar Shafawi when following Meem Sakinah?
Which two letters are EXCLUDED from Izhar Shafawi?
How should a vowelless Meem be pronounced during Izhar Shafawi?
options: Clearly and distinctly without merging or holding a nasal Ghunnah

assessment_bank.question: Why is extra care required when Izhar Shafawi occurs before the letter Waw (و) or Fa (ف)?
options: Because Waw and Fa share lip proximity, making reciters prone to mistakenly hiding the Meem (Ikhfa)
Because Waw and Fa are throat letters
Because the Meem turns into a Baa

assessment_bank.question: In the phrase 'عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا', what rule applies between Meem and Waw?
What is the visual sign of Meem Sakinah in the Mushaf during Izhar Shafawi?
options: A clear Sukoon sign (مْ) placed above the Meem
A bare Meem with no sign

assessment_bank.question: In 'أَمْ لَمْ تُنْذِرْهُمْ', how is the Meem of 'أَمْ' pronounced before Lam?
options: Clearly with its inherent sound, no Ghunnah hold

assessment_bank.question: What common error do students commit when reciting 'عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا'?
options: Incorrectly applying Ikhfa due to the close lip articulation of Waw
Turning the Meem into a Noon

assessment_bank.question: Can Izhar Shafawi occur across two words as well as within a single word?
options: Yes, it occurs in both cases
Only at the end of an Ayah

assessment_bank.question: Summarize the core requirement of Izhar Shafawi:
options: Pronounce Meem Sakinah clearly and crisply before any letter except Baa and Meem, maintaining zero nasal holding
Convert the Meem to a Meem Mushaddadah
